data.narrative:
Halo is a Series B semiconductor company founded by Andrei Iancu, Philip Van Stockum, and Charlie Rudy, having raised $122M to date. The valuation analysis draws from a comparative universe of 3 public semiconductors (ALAB, NVDA, AMD) and 8 private frontier-chip companies at Series A through Series C, including stage peers Positron AI and adjacent-stage comparables Rebellions, d-Matrix, and DEEPX.

Two valuation methods are applicable. Stage-progression analysis applies a 1.9x step-up multiplier typical for Series B advancement, yielding $232M. Peer-median anchoring across four same-sector, same/adjacent-stage companies produces $1.5B, reflecting a range of $529M (DEEPX, Series C) to $2.3B (Rebellions, Series A). Public-comp P/S anchoring cannot be applied; the public semiconductor sector trades at a 20.4x median multiple, but Halo's revenue is not disclosed and private semiconductor companies rarely disclose this metric.

The triangulated valuation range is $197M (low), $866M (median), and $1.7B (high). This wide dispersion reflects material uncertainty around stage-specific growth expectations and heterogeneity within the peer set across funding stages. The peer-median method carries greater weight given the robust private comparables, though the gap between stage-progression and peer-median results highlights sensitivity to whether Halo's trajectory tracks early-stage outliers (Rebellions, d-Matrix) or more measured comparable growth.
